summary: To promote the place of women in research and technology in France, the Irène Joliot-Curie Prize was created for 2018. Registrations close on June 15.
requirements: Must fit into one of the three award categories (Femme scientifique de l’année, Jeune Femme scientifique, or Femme, recherche et entreprise).
Foreign applicants must reside in France.
benefits: Total prize endowment of 70,000 euros in 2018 split across the three award categories.
National and international recognition of research achievements.
eligibility: Open to women with exemplary careers/paths in research and technology combining excellence and dynamism.
Open to foreign female researchers who reside in France (attributed without nationality conditions).
Category 1 ('Femme scientifique de l’année'): Women who have made a remarkable contribution in public research through significant work and national/international recognition.

Category 3 ('Femme, recherche et entreprise'): Women who have developed society-benefiting innovations working within a company or contributing to company creation.
howToApply: Consult the regulations ('Consulter le règlement') referenced on the source portal.
Complete registration before the stated deadline (June 15).
selectionProcess: Evaluated across three categories: 'Femme scientifique de l’année', 'Jeune Femme scientifique', and 'Femme, recherche et entreprise'.
Selection emphasizes exemplary careers combining excellence and dynamism, public research contributions, specialist leadership, or business/societal innovation.
aiSummary: The Irène Joliot-Curie Award (Prix Irène Joliot-Curie) was created to promote the role of women in research and technology in France. livingAllowance: Included in the £22,050 annual maintenance allowance.
travelSupport: One economy single airfare at both the beginning and end of the course.
benefits: Full-cost coverage of the University Composition Fee (at the appropriate rate).
Maintenance allowance for a single student (£22,050 for 12 months at the 2025-26 rate; pro rata for shorter courses; funded up to 4 years for PhD scholars).
One economy single airfare at both the beginning and end of the course.
Inbound visa costs and the cost of the Immigration Health Surcharge.
Discretionary academic development funding (from up to £750 to up to £4,000 dependent on course length) for conferences and courses.
Discretionary Dependent Children Allowance (up to £12,793 per annum for one child; up to £18,244 per annum for two or more children).
Discretionary fieldwork maintenance support (keep up to normal maintenance allowance while on PhD fieldwork).
Discretionary maternity/paternity funding (intermit studies for up to 6 months while continuing maintenance allowance).
Discretionary hardship funding for unforeseen difficulties.
eligibility: Applicants must be from countries outside the UK.
Must be applying to pursue a postgraduate degree (including PhDs) in any subject available at the University of Cambridge.
howToApply: Apply for a postgraduate degree at the University of Cambridge following the University's application route (refer to the Graduate Studies prospectus for fee details).
Notify the Trust as soon as possible if awarded any other funding towards your degree at Cambridge.
selectionProcess: Candidates are evaluated based on four core criteria: outstanding intellectual ability, reasons for choice of course, commitment to improving the lives of others, and leadership potential.
Awards are distributed across two selection rounds: the US round (approximately 25 awards) and the International round (approximately 55 awards).
aiSummary: The Gates Cambridge Scholarship is a fully funded postgraduate scholarship designed to build a global network of future leaders committed to improving the lives of others. The program provides full-cost funding for outstanding applicants from countries outside the UK to pursue a postgraduate degree (including PhDs) in any subject available at the University of Cambridge. Core funding covers the University Composition Fee, a single-student maintenance allowance (£22,050 for 12 months at the 2025-26 rate, up to 4 years for PhDs), economy airfares at the beginning and end of the course, and inbound visa/Immigration Health Surcharge costs. Discretionary funding is available for academic development, dependent children, fieldwork maintenance, maternity/paternity leave, and hardship. Selection is based on outstanding intellectual ability, choice of course, commitment to improving the lives of others, and leadership potential.
aiRequirements: Demonstrate outstanding intellectual ability.
Provide clear reasons for choice of course.
Demonstrate a commitment to improving the lives of others.
Demonstrate leadership potential.
aiActions: Check specific department fee details in the Cambridge Graduate Studies prospectus.
Prepare application materials highlighting leadership, academic achievement, choice of course, and commitment to social impact.
Verify exact application deadlines and entry requirements directly on the official source or department portal.
aiSelectionSignals: Strong evidence of outstanding academic performance and intellectual ability.
A well-articulated rationale for selecting the specific course at the University of Cambridge.
Proven track record demonstrating a commitment to improving the lives of others.
Clear evidence of leadership potential and impact.
aiRisks: Failure to disclose other sources of funding or employer salaries as required by the Trust.
Bench fees and academic equipment/resource costs are not covered by the scholarship and must be provided by the academic department.
No funding or allowance is provided for a partner.
aiFundingNotes: The scholarship covers full core costs plus discretionary components. If a student receives a fee award from public authorities (such as UKRI), they must accept it, and the Trust will not pay their fee or may share fee and maintenance costs. The Trust reserves the right to reduce or eliminate the maintenance allowance if the scholar receives an employer salary or another substantial scholarship. The scholarship does not cover bench fees, scientific equipment, or similar academic resources, which are expected to be covered by the academic department at Cambridge.
